es.summary: Una identidad de AWS eliminó con éxito un bucket de S3, según CloudTrail. Puede ser limpieza autorizada o destrucción de datos y borrado de evidencias por parte de un atacante.
es.what_it_detects: Eventos de CloudTrail con eventName igual a DeleteBucket cuyo errorCode está vacío o es 'Success', es decir, eliminaciones de buckets que se completaron. Los intentos fallidos, como AccessDenied, no se detectan.
es.why_it_matters: Al eliminar un bucket se pierden sus datos de forma permanente y se puede borrar evidencia, como logs de CloudTrail o de acceso guardados en S3. La regla está etiquetada en la táctica Stealth (evasión) de ATT&CK.
triage_steps: Identifique el bucket en requestParameters.bucketName y determine su propósito: logs de CloudTrail, backups, datos de producción o recursos de prueba.
Revise userIdentity (arn, type, accessKeyId) para saber si es un usuario humano, un rol asumido o una cuenta de servicio, y quién es su responsable.
Valide sourceIPAddress, userAgent y awsRegion frente a la actividad habitual de esa identidad. Desconfíe de IPs nuevas, de herramientas de CLI inusuales o de regiones atípicas.
Busque eventos previos de la misma identidad en ±15 minutos: DeleteObjects, PutBucketLifecycleConfiguration, PutBucketPolicy, StopLogging, DeleteTrail o UpdateTrail.
Verifique si el bucket era destino de algún trail, de logs de acceso o de VPC Flow Logs. Si lo era, trate el caso como posible borrado de evidencias.
Revise eventos anteriores de la misma sesión: ConsoleLogin, AssumeRole, CreateAccessKey o GetObject masivos que sugieran exfiltración antes del borrado.
Confirme con el dueño del bucket, o con el ticket de cambio, si la eliminación estaba planificada.
false_positives: Administradores autorizados que eliminan buckets durante tareas de mantenimiento, limpieza o pruebas.
Pipelines de IaC (Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK) que destruyen entornos efímeros o de staging.
Automatizaciones de ciclo de vida que eliminan buckets temporales de builds o de análisis.
response_steps: Verifique con el responsable de la identidad y del bucket antes de tomar cualquier acción; documente el ticket de cambio si existe.
Si no está autorizado, desactive las access keys implicadas y revoque las sesiones activas del rol o del usuario.
Analice toda la actividad de esa identidad en CloudTrail para encontrar persistencia: usuarios, keys o roles nuevos, y cambios en políticas.
Restaure los datos desde réplicas, AWS Backup o copias externas. Vuelva a crear el bucket para que nadie más pueda registrar ese nombre.
Restablezca el logging si se vio afectado y limite s3:DeleteBucket mediante SCP o políticas de bucket para los recursos críticos.
es.severity_rationale: Medium es adecuado: la acción tiene un impacto alto si es maliciosa, pero es una operación administrativa frecuente que requiere contexto para confirmarla.

en.summary: CloudTrail shows that an AWS identity successfully deleted an S3 bucket. This may be authorized cleanup, or an attacker destroying data and removing evidence.
en.what_it_detects: CloudTrail events with eventName DeleteBucket where errorCode is empty or 'Success', meaning bucket deletions that completed. Failed attempts such as AccessDenied are not matched.
en.why_it_matters: Deleting a bucket permanently removes its data and can wipe evidence such as CloudTrail or access logs stored in S3. The rule is tagged under the ATT&CK Stealth (evasion) tactic.
triage_steps: Identify the bucket from requestParameters.bucketName and its purpose: CloudTrail logs, backups, production data or test resources.
Review userIdentity (arn, type, accessKeyId) to tell whether it is a human user, an assumed role or a service account, and find the owner.
Compare sourceIPAddress, userAgent and awsRegion with the identity's usual activity. Treat new IPs, unusual CLI tools or atypical regions as suspicious.
Search the same identity within +/- 15 minutes for DeleteObjects, PutBucketLifecycleConfiguration, PutBucketPolicy, StopLogging, DeleteTrail or UpdateTrail.
Check whether the bucket was a destination for a trail, access logs or VPC Flow Logs. If it was, treat the case as possible evidence removal.
Review earlier events in the same session, such as ConsoleLogin, AssumeRole, CreateAccessKey or bulk GetObject, that would suggest exfiltration before the deletion.
Confirm with the bucket owner or the change ticket that the deletion was planned.
false_positives: Authorized administrators deleting buckets during maintenance, cleanup or testing.
IaC pipelines (Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK) tearing down ephemeral or staging environments.
Lifecycle automation that removes temporary build or analytics buckets.
response_steps: Check with the owners of the identity and the bucket before acting, and record the change ticket if there is one.
If the deletion was not authorized, disable the access keys involved and revoke the role's or user's active sessions.
Review all CloudTrail activity for that identity to find persistence: new users, keys or roles, and policy changes.
Restore the data from replicas, AWS Backup or external copies. Recreate the bucket so no one else can register that name.
Turn logging back on if it was affected, and restrict s3:DeleteBucket on critical resources with SCPs or bucket policies.
en.severity_rationale: Medium fits: a malicious deletion has high impact, but deleting buckets is a common admin task, so context is needed to confirm it.

positive.description: Successful DeleteBucket with no errorCode, made by an IAM user through the AWS CLI from an unusual IP
DeleteBucket by an assumed role with errorCode explicitly set to Success

negative.description: DeleteBucket attempt that failed with AccessDenied, so neither status selection matches
Successful DeleteBucketPolicy, a different event name that only partly matches
